Software & Web Development – Full-stack applications, websites, platforms, and UI/UX design projects. 2. Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML) – Data-driven solutions, predictive models, natural language processing, and intelligent systems. 3. Cybersecurity – Ethical hacking, security tools, vulnerability detection, and secure system design. Problem Statements Release: Official problem statements under each domain will be shared with registered teams on the day of the event. • Rule: No Internet connection allowed. • Problem statements will be provided at the start. • Teams must create a comprehensive design document including UI/UX screens (hand-drawn or digital), user roles/responsibilities, database schema/ER diagrams, tech stack selection, and unique planned features. • Disqualification: Failure for Submitting COMPLETE design requirements within 4 hours. Round 2: Implementation Round (18 Hours) • Rule: Internet usage and personal devices (laptops, mobile phones) are permitted. • Shortlisted teams bring their ideas to life by building working prototypes based on the Round 1 design document. • Must feature working frontend/backend integration, database mapping, and key functionality. • Prepare a presentation outlining implementation steps, technical challenges, and key components. • Disqualification: Failure to produce a working model

• Prepare a presentation outlining implementation steps, technical challenges, and key components. • Disqualification: Failure to produce a working model or missing implementation criteria. Round 3: Presentation Round (2 Hours) • Selected teams present their working solutions to a panel of judges. • Includes a live demo, process explanation, and a Q&A session regarding technical choices and future scope. Round 4: Closing Ceremony & Prizes • Announcement of top 3 teams, prize distribution, and issuing of participation certificates for all. Rules & Regulations 4.1 Eligibility & Team Formation • Student Status: Open to currently enrolled undergraduate or postgraduate engineering students. • Verification: Valid student ID or official proof of enrollment is mandatory. • Team Size: Individual entries or teams of 2 to 4 members are permitted. Interdisciplinary and multi- year teams are allowed. • Leadership & Roster: Each team must designate a team leader. No team changes are allowed after the event starts. • Exclusivity: Organizers, sponsors, family members, or students registered in multiple teams are non- eligible. 4.2 Registration & Identification • Identity Proof: Participants must carry both their college ID and a hard copy of a government- verified ID (e.g., Aadhaar, Driving License, Passport). • Consent Form: A

college ID and a hard copy of a government- verified ID (e.g., Aadhaar, Driving License, Passport). • Consent Form: A signed hardcopy consent form from a parent or guardian is strictly mandatory for all participants. 4.3 Equipment & Amenities • Hardware: Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers and extension board. • Connectivity: The venue will provide continuous access to power outlets and stable Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity. • Provided Meals: Lunch, snacks, and dinner will be provided on October 10th. Breakfast will be provided on October 11th. 4.4 Project Development Guidelines • Originality: All projects must be original and built entirely during the 24-hour hackathon period. • Alignment: Projects must strictly align with the provided themes or approved problem statements.
